clue.text: Country girl following bachelor's lead

indicators.note: the girl comes after the bachelor's letter, so her name is written second
a word's lead is its first letter, so take the front of the word bachelor

parts.note: Olivia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A country girl trails behind a single man who is setting the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a landlocked nation in South America, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: A bird a doctor reared is under arrest

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under places these letters below the first piece

parts.note: a bust is a police raid or arrest

indicators.note: reared up means stood up, turning the letters upwards in a down entry

explanation.surface: A bird raised by a vet finds itself in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reared' turns the doctor round, as a down entry reads upwards; 'is under' sets the bird's tail below the arrest. The opening 'A' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large ground-dwelling game bird of open country.

clue.text: Small child wearing cap is kept within bounds

indicators.note: a lid worn sits round the child, so the child goes inside

parts.note: a lid is a cap or cover
a mite is a little child

explanation.surface: A toddler made to wear a hat is not allowed to wander.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited means restricted, confined inside fixed limits.

clue.text: These statistics show lesbianism's origin is post-Sackville-West

indicators.note: post means after, so the letter is placed after the name

parts.note: Vita Sackville-West was an English writer

indicators.note: a word's origin is its first letter

explanation.surface: Figures about lesbianism's beginnings dating from after Vita Sackville-West's time.
explanation.walkthrough: Vita Sackville-West was a writer famed for her affair with Virginia Woolf, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital statistics are a person's body measurements, the phrase the clue completes.

clue.text: Schools whence ideas came?

indicators.note: whence asks where the letters came from, so the schools are built from those words rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering which colleges gave rise to certain notions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue nods at the Academy of Plato, a school that was a source of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Academies are schools, especially private or specialist ones.

clue.text: Letter from Lysander about a dance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the Greek letter is placed round the single letter

parts.note: Lysander was a Spartan, so his letter is a Greek one: lambda

explanation.surface: Someone receives a note from Lysander concerning a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence, but a Greek general's letter is a character of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian partner dance popular in the late 1980s.

clue.text: Not even a smoker on the outskirts of Pitlochry

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the smoker above the next letters

parts.note: lum is Scots for a chimney, something that smokes

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rough road beside a chimney on the edge of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitlochry is a Scottish town, hinting at the Scots word LUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumpy means uneven, full of bumps.

clue.text: Enigma not puzzling essayist

indicators.note: puzzling suggests confusion, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle that is not baffling for a writer of essays.
explanation.definitionFit: Michel de Montaigne was the French writer who invented the essay form.

clue.text: Noted place for bridge from six to midnight, stopping soon

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the time span goes inside

parts.note: anon means soon
VI is six in Roman numerals
the middle of the word night is G

explanation.surface: A card game played from early evening to midnight is about to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game, but it is the famous Pont d'Avignon of the French song.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon has a famous broken medieval bridge celebrated in a French nursery song.

clue.text: Name successor in speech

definitions.meaning: in the stock phrase name and ..., this is what follows name
a formal talk to an audience

explanation.definitionFit: Address comes after name in the familiar phrase, and a formal speech is also an address.

clue.text: Island scholar delving into Sanskrit sayings

indicators.note: to delve into something is to go inside it, so the scholar goes within the sayings

parts.note: a sutra is a Sanskrit aphorism or collection of them
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree

explanation.surface: An academic researches Sanskrit aphorisms concerning an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large island in western Indonesia.

clue.text: Where Americans fought over child in German race

indicators.note: in an across clue, over signals the word turned round from end to start

parts.note: Nam is the American slang name for Vietnam, scene of the war
Kind is the German word for child

explanation.surface: A soldier fought over a child in a German race.
explanation.definitionFit: Mankind is the human race, the whole species taken together.

clue.text: Major road blocked by evil gunmen

indicators.note: a road blocked by something has it sitting in its middle, so evil goes inside the road

parts.note: an artery is a main traffic route
ill can mean evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: A main road has been barricaded by wicked men with guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery also names the soldiers who man the big guns, a collective term for gunners.

clue.text: Making a comeback in "White Horse Inn", a musical heroine

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in reverse, so the letters are read right to left
the answer sits inside the quoted words, running across them

explanation.surface: A heroine from an operetta returns to the stage in White Horse Inn.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'Horse Inn, a' are the letters EINNA, which 'Making a comeback' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is the orphan who is the title heroine of the Broadway musical about Little Orphan Annie.

clue.text: Trick automobile manufacturer

explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty trick, and Dodge is also a US maker of cars.

clue.text: Swans I see in river requiring a lot of bread

indicators.note: in places the birds and their companions inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
pens are female swans
v, for vide, means see

explanation.surface: Seeing swans on a river that need a lot of feeding.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, not food for swans.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expensive costs a lot of money, bread being slang for cash.

clue.text: Natives of exotic locations with inside information

indicators.note: with the information inside means it is placed within the locations

parts.note: the Indies, East or West, stand for faraway exotic places
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Locals in faraway places have the inside story.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigenes are people native to a place, the original inhabitants.

clue.text: He thought he was a philosopher

definitions.text: He thought he was a philosopher

parts.words: He thought he was a philosopher
parts.note: alludes to the famous saying I think, therefore I am, a thinker whose existence came from his thinking

explanation.definitionFit: Descartes wrote cogito ergo sum, holding that thinking proved he existed.

clue.text: Silent brothers, very quiet in dire straits

indicators.note: in places the musical marking inside the rearranged letters
dire suggests something in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: Monks under a vow of silence keep their peace even in great hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' gives TRAISTS from the strait letters, and the musical very-quiet marking goes inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappists are Cistercian monks known for keeping a strict rule of silence.

clue.text: Deal with jam maker

definitions.meaning: to deal in goods is to trade in them
a jam on the roads is caused by heavy vehicle flow

explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as a verb means trade, and road traffic causes jams.

clue.text: A mate getting married in the short term?

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or mate

explanation.surface: A friend gets married on short notice.
explanation.definitionFit: An acronym is an abbreviation formed from initial letters, a shortened term.

clue.text: Dear friend's letters regularly went astray

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: A close friend's correspondence was going missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second, fourth and so on letters of DEARFRIENDS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to stray from the right path, so erred means wandered off course.

clue.text: Screen left out when joiner turns up

indicators.note: left out means the left letter is removed
in a down clue, turning up reverses the letters

parts.note: a solderer joins metals

explanation.surface: A screen is abandoned when the carpenter arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses SOLDERER to REREDLOS; 'out' removes L.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Unsteady female coming round day after day on railway

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
the female goes round, so the days sit inside her

parts.note: a doe is a female deer

indicators.note: one day is placed after the other

parts.note: D again for day
D again for day

explanation.surface: A shaky woman visits day after day by train.
explanation.definitionFit: Doddery means shaky and unsteady, especially through age.

clue.text: In favour of an outer garment

indicators.note: outer says the little word goes on the outside, wrapping the other piece

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone argues in favour of an outer garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a protective piece of clothing tied over the front of the body.

clue.text: In love — with sweetheart weaving around me

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

indicators.note: weaving moves strands in and out, so the letters are interlaced into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A besotted person dances with a lover circling about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enamoured means being smitten or captivated, filled with romantic feeling.

clue.text: New student's missing father somewhere in Surrey

indicators.note: missing means without, so the father's letters are removed

parts.note: a fresher is a new university student
Fr is the abbreviation for father, a priest

explanation.surface: A first-year student is without a father in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Esher is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a town in the English county of Surrey.

clue.text: Love some modern paintings

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of some modern art.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s style of abstract painting exploiting optical effects.

clue.text: Perhaps sole repository for local language

indicators.note: a repository holds things, so the fish contains the pub

parts.note: sole is an example of a fish, as perhaps signals
a local is a British pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A fish may be where a regional dialect is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is the pub nearest your home in Britain. 'local language' wants to be read together, but local is the inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnish is the national tongue of Finland.

clue.text: Funny walk seen on telly originally? Nonsense!

indicators.note: the walk is placed after the first letter, building on it
originally points to the start of the word telly

parts.note: a waddle is a comic, swaying walk like a duck's

explanation.surface: A comic gait broadcast on television is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly, trivial talk or writing, a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Turn up right outside gym for social match

indicators.note: the arrival and the right go round the gym, which sits inside

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive or come
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: Someone appears at the gym to find a partner for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is an equal in rank or a companion, someone who matches you socially.

clue.text: Convince with shaking fist, say?

indicators.note: shaking scrambles the letters of fist and say

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to win an argument by brandishing a fist.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone can mean to persuade them fully that something is true.
